messages.content: Predict this participant’s actual response. Four real people with anonymous labels A, B, C, D play a public goods game. Each round each person has an endowment of 400 euro cents (4 euros) and privately contributes 0–400 cents in steps of 2 cents to a common fund, keeping the rest. The fund is doubled and split equally among all four: before punishment, a person earns 400 minus their own contribution plus half the sum of all four contributions. Contributions are simultaneous and other people’s current contributions are unknown when contributing. A later punishment opportunity is announced before contributions. After contributions, participants estimate contributions, then see all four contributions, their sum and the four current incomes. Each person can spend their earned money on punishment: 1 cent of personal cost reduces a selected other person’s payoff by 4 cents. Others can also punish you. A separate Yes/No gate asks whether to punish at least one other member. Yes (space bar) opens a later screen to enter costs toward three other people jointly; No (Enter) skips this amount screen and spending is automatically zero. Amounts denote personal cost, not the fourfold damage. Positive-gate amounts may include zero; a Yes followed by a zero vector remains a Yes gate. Monetary results are paid after the study; the local primary material does not specify a fixed fee. The interaction is repeated with the same partners and stable anonymous labels, allowing reputation and deterrence. The exact future ending announced to participants is not established in the released material.  Return only the contributed amount in euro cents: one even integer from 0 to 400.

You are player A. You are at the contribution decision in round 1. Your new contribution endowment is 400 cents. No current peer contributions are yet shown.
